planting.note: Plant tubers once soil has warmed in spring; waterlily types benefit from staking as stems lengthen.

directions: 'Cameo' is a classic waterlily-flowered dahlia producing fully double, flat to saucer-shaped blooms of soft pale yellow aging to cream, with broad, slightly cupped outer florets that give the flower its delicate, open-faced waterlily form. Strong stems hold the blooms well above compact, bushy foliage, making it a favorite for cutting. Grow in full sun with even moisture, stake in windy sites, and lift tubers after the first fall frost in climates where the ground freezes.

planting.note: Plant tubers after danger of frost has passed; tall stems appreciate support in exposed beds.

directions: 'Polka' is an anemone-flowered dahlia with creamy white outer petals edged in rose-cranberry surrounding a dense, pincushion-like center of golden-yellow tubular florets, the outer petals blushing deeper pink as each bloom matures so that no two flowers look quite alike. Plants grow tall with long, sturdy stems well suited to cutting gardens. Provide full sun and consistent moisture, stake in windy locations, and lift and store tubers over winter where frost occurs.

planting.note: An early-blooming, vigorous anemone type; stake the tall stems at planting time.

directions: 'Alpen Fury' is a tall, vigorous anemone-flowered dahlia bearing a bright golden-yellow pincushion center domed above a surrounding ring of broad red ray florets, creating a bold, open-faced bicolor bloom roughly four to six inches across. It blooms earlier in the season than many large dahlias and continues steadily into fall. Grow in full sun with sturdy staking for its height, and lift tubers after frost blackens the foliage in cold-winter climates.

planting.note: RHS Award of Garden Merit winner; dark bronze foliage contrasts well with bedding partners.

directions: 'Magenta Star' is a single/star-flowered dahlia bearing a single outer ring of vivid magenta petals around a dark reddish-brown disc rimmed in gold, set off by distinctive purplish-bronze foliage. It flowers prolifically from midsummer until frost and holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, valued for both garden display and pollinator visits. Grow in full sun, water during dry spells, and lift tubers for winter storage in regions with freezing winters.

planting.note: Tall anemone type; stake at planting and support as stems lengthen.

directions: 'Platinum Blonde' is an anemone-flowered dahlia with crisp pure white outer petals surrounding a dense, feather-textured center of creamy yellow tubular florets, giving a luminous two-toned bloom on strong upright stems. Its clean color combination makes it a popular choice for cutting gardens and mixed borders alike. Grow in full sun with regular moisture, stake for support, and lift tubers after frost in cold climates to overwinter indoors.
